Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Nexus Energy Corp's Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Steve Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; David Kim, Chief Strategy Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Technology Officer; and Robert Patel, Chief Regulatory Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1.  Strong operational performance in our generation fleet.
    2.  Continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio.
    3.  Effective cost management.
    4.  Progress on our infrastructure investments.
    5.  Successful integration of Desert Peak hybrid facility.
    6.  Advancement of our net-zero by 2045 pathway program.
    7.  Positive regulatory outcomes in PJM.

Let me provide some more detail on these seven key aspects. First, our generation fleet posted record capacity factors, particularly in nuclear and renewables, amid hotter weather boosting demand. Second, renewables added significant capacity, with projects like Lone Star Solar advancing toward completion. Third, we kept costs in check through hedging and efficiency gains. Fourth, infrastructure spend is fueling rate base growth. Fifth, the Desert Peak integration with bifacial modules and iron-air storage is yielding early wins. Sixth, our net-zero efforts are accelerating with IRA support. And seventh, PJM approvals are unlocking key projects.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Steve Harlan to discuss the financials in depth.

Steve Harlan: Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. For the Q3, we reported adjusted diluted earnings per share of $1.28 and revenue of $2.52 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model—spanning thermal, renewables, and nuclear across PJM, ERCOT, and CAISO markets serving 5 million customers—and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Let me start with an overview of our results relative to guidance and prior periods. We exceeded our Q3 guidance across the board. Consolidated revenues hit $2.52 billion, up 8.7% from $2.32 billion in Q3 2023 and 4.2% sequentially from Q2's $2.42 billion, beating our midpoint by about 7.6% or $205 million. This came from stronger retail sales up 4.2% to 28.4 million MWh on hotter cooling degrees, plus merchant upside in PJM and ERCOT where prices averaged $48 per MWh, up 12% year-over-year on data center demand. Adjusted EBITDA reached $812 million, 11.1% above last year's $731 million and 6.8% over Q2's $760 million, expanding margins to 37% thanks to fuel at $22.50 per MWh, down 8%, with 85% gas hedged at $3.75 per MMBtu. Adjusted EPS of $1.28 was 13.6% over prior year and 9% above guidance, while net income was $425 million or $1.15 per share.

Generation, 62% of EBITDA, delivered $585 million, up 14.2% year-over-year on 18.2 million MWh generated, up 7.1%, with wind at 38% capacity factor and solar at 24.5% including new Desert Sun Phase II. Transmission & Distribution added $227 million, flat year-over-year but up sequentially on data center volumes. Fuel and O&M held at 28% of revenues through hedging and synergies. Texas led with 16% revenue growth to $1.05 billion on scarcity pricing and $45 million battery ancillaries. Full-year guidance raised: adjusted EBITDA $3.25-3.35 billion, up from prior range and 9-12% over 2023; EPS $4.90-$5.10.

Turning to our capital expenditure plan, which underpins regulated rate base growth, clean transition, and load demands from electrification and data centers. We're affirming FY2024 CAPEX at $7.8 billion, up 12% from 2023's $6.9 billion and midpoint of our $38 billion five-year plan through 2028, with $450 million AFUDC aiding 7-9% CAGR rate base growth. Year-to-date through Q3, $5.9 billion deployed, 76% of plan, ahead on renewables.

By category, renewables and grid mod at 55% or $4.3 billion roughly annualized. Renewables: 45% or $3.5 billion, with 4.2 GW pipeline targeting 10 GW by 2028. ERCOT's 800 MW Lone Star Solar + Storage 85% complete, $1.1 billion including 400 MWh BESS, 12-year PPA at $45/MWh effective with PTC, IRR over 12%, 98% early factor. Offshore: 50% stake in 1,200 MW Atlantic Breeze, $2.4 billion gross, 60% foundations, Vestas 15 MW turbines, first power H2 2026 with NJ ZREC and 30% ITC. Emerging: 200 MW First Solar bifacial PERC-plus at Desert Peak with 100 MWh Form Energy iron-air storage for duck curve.

Transmission & Distribution: 35% or $2.7 billion. PJM RTEP $3.2 billion through 2027; $850 million Mid-Atlantic HVDC Spine 40% done, +2,000 MW transfer. CAISO $450 million wildfire mit, 1,500 miles covered conductor, 75% risk cut. Smart grid $300 million ADMS/DERMS for 20% more solar integration.

Nuclear & Thermal: 15% or $1.2 billion. 2,200 MW fleet 93.2% factor; $600 million Salem Harbor life extension like Palisades, NRC filed for 2046. Gas $250 million H2 blending to 30% by 2026; NuScale MoU for 300 MW PJM SMR.

Other 5% $400 million, including $150 million for 50,000 EV chargers under VGI tariff. ERCOT merchant peaks at $200/MWh; regulated 9-10% returns. Challenges like 8% steel up, labor delays mitigated by Siemens/Bechtel deals. 3.5x debt/EBITDA strong. Fuels 6-8% EPS growth, $1.2 billion IRA value.

On dividend policy, it's core to our shareholder covenant, with 68 years uninterrupted like Southern Co. Annualized $2.64/share, 4.1% yield, targeting 3-5% growth. Payout 60-75% adjusted EPS, 70-80% FCFE; Q3 TTM 68% EPS, 72% FCFE. Historical: EPS from $5.28 '21 to $6.45 TTM, dividend $2.40 to $2.64, coverage 2.4x. 6% five-year CAGR. Funds $12-14 billion annual capex: 70% dividends, 20% debt/pension, 10% buybacks ($150 million YTD of $500 million). Supports clean energy like 2 GW solar-storage, SMR, HVDC. Southeast data centers, Midwest wind hedged. 2025-27 guide 4-6% growth to $2.95/share, 65-70% payout on 5-7% EPS growth.

Regulatory lag—delay in recovering costs like 18% fuel up to $1.2 billion in 2023, opex inflation—dragged EEM 220 bps last year, average 9-12 months. PJM 55% rate base slower FRT; ERCOT <6 months LMP. Mitigations: Virginia $425 million settlement 92% ask with capex rider for 800 MW BESS. Fuel trackers 70% jurisdictions 95% in 90 days; PA decoupling. $2.5 billion 2024 capex front-loaded for CWIP ROE uplift; Siemens dispatch cut fuel 14%, hydrogen pilots. Advocacy for PBR, hedges 85% gas at $3.25/MMBtu. Lag narrowed to 7 months Q2, ROE 9.8-10.2% 2024.

Before outlook, forward-looking statements subject to risks like gas prices, supply chains for turbines, FERC changes, rates on $15 billion maturities, weather, IRA shifts—see 10-K/Q. FY2025 EBITDA $2.55-2.75 billion, 8-12% growth, EPS $4.05-4.45. Load 6-8% CAGR; 1.2 GW new PPAs at $65/MWh effective $45 all-in. 2.3 GW 2025: 1.4 GW solar +900 MW/3.6 GWh BESS, 900 MW wind; $250 million ITC transfer. 5 GW by 2027 incl. iron-air, H2. Nuclear uprate 150 MW Diablo Canyon +$180 million EBITDA; gas 40-50% factors. CAISO NEM 3.0 arbitrage; ERCOT peakers; DOE grid support. $1.5 billion asset sales. ROE 10-12% reg, 15%+ unreg. Sensitivities: +10% rates -$0.15 EPS; $4 gas +$100 million EBITDA. 10%+ EPS CAGR.

Capex Q3 $450 million toward $1.8-7.8 billion full-year depending on program, 55% renewables/storage, 30% T&D, 15% thermal. Balance sheet solid: 3.2x net debt/EBITDA, $2.4 billion liquidity. Q4 generation 17.5-18.5 million MWh at $55-60/MWh, 88% hedged. 2025 initial: 8-10% EBITDA growth to $3.5-3.7 billion on 1 GW COD, 800 MW data centers, wider spreads. Executing Reliable Renewables Plus with 650 MW clean YTD.

Steve Harlan: Thank you. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders through our 65% dividend payout.

Now, over to Maria for operations.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Steve. On operations, we're seeing improved efficiency in our combined cycle gas turbine power plants due to AI predictive maintenance implementation. This has resulted in a 5% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 15%, thanks to digital optimizations across our 25 GW fleet hitting 94% availability, with nuclear at 93.5% and renewables strong on new solar-storage CODs.

David Kim: Thank you, Maria. For strategy, we're exploring small modular reactors and long-duration storage. SMR MoUs with NuScale for 300 MW by 2030, and evaluating acquisitions in ERCOT for merchant gas amid 15% load CAGR from AI data centers per EIA.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, David. Technologically, investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity include deploying advanced threat detection platforms to bolster defenses. We're piloting advanced distribution management systems in CAISO for DER integration and AI dispatch.

Robert Patel: Thank you, Lisa. Regulatorily, we received approval for our grid resilience rider in PJM. This allows full recovery of $450 million in hardening capex at 10.2% ROE.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Steve, Maria, David, Lisa, and Robert. In summary, solid execution across the board. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks. Good morning, team. Could you walk us through the details on your storm response and recovery efforts from Hurricane Epsilon last quarter? Specifically, how that's flowing through to costs, restoration metrics, and any updates on your grid hardening initiatives?

Alex Rivera: Good morning, Sarah. Happy to dive into this. Hurricane Epsilon hit as a Category 3 across our Southeast territory on October 15th, 120 mph winds, 12-foot surges in Georgia and Carolinas, top-10 impact affecting 2.8 million customers or 65% of regional retail base over 45,000 square miles.

Pre-landfall 48 hours, activated NERC-aligned plan, mobilized 4,200 lineworkers including 2,100 mutual aid from Duke, Southern, Oncor—25% more than Delta. 150 drone crews with FLIR LiDAR/thermal cut inspections 40%. Peak 1.95 million out at 2 a.m. Day 1, 55% restored EOD Day 1, 95% by Hour 72, full by Day 5. SAIDI 285 minutes vs. 335 average, 15% better; SAIFI 1.8. DER areas like Carolinas under 48 hours for 80%.

Georgia 1.2 million out, 3,200 poles, 450 miles conductor on 69 kV. Carolinas flooding 15 substations, elevated switchgear helped. Florida minimal.

Financials: $285 million gross; opex $145 million (labor $85M, materials $40M Hubbell composites, logistics $20M); capex $140 million rebuilds over 85% threshold. $210 million insurance net of deducts, 70% approved—$75 million net Q4 EBITDA hit, 8% guidance.

Accelerating $2.2 billion five-year resilience: 1,200 miles undergrounding coastal by 2027 (350 miles done, 60% risk cut ASCE 7-22); 85% AMI, AutoGrid AI predicted 75% faults; 50 MW Fluence BESS black-start; LiDAR veg every 3 years cut tree outs 30%. GA 95% pass-through rider; Carolinas filing $450 million surcharge like FPL. Weather up 25% NOAA; capex to 18% rate base. Guidance reaffirmed $1.85-1.95 EPS storm-normalized, 6-8% growth.

Sarah, does that cover it?

Sarah Jenkins: That's comprehensive—thanks, Alex.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Larson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Larson: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for CAPEX allocation next year?

Alex Rivera: Certainly, Mike. As Steve detailed, we're sticking to $7.8 billion pace, heavy renewables and T&D to hit 10 GW clean adds by 2028, with strong returns from PPAs and IRA.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: What is your outlook for regulatory lag impacts?

Steve Harlan: Solid question. We've narrowed it to 7 months through riders, trackers, and CWIP, targeting under 6 by 2025 with ROE expansion to 10.5%.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly: How are you mitigating risks related to dividend sustainability amid capex ramp?

Maria Gonzalez: We're balancing with strong FCFE coverage at 2.4x, 70% regulated stability, and hedges ensuring payouts stay 65-70% even in stress scenarios.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Nexus Energy Corp for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Nexus Energy Corp.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
